questions.question: What does dp[i][j] represent in the LCS problem?
options: Length of longest common substring ending at i and j
Length of LCS of text1[0:i] and text2[0:j]
Minimum operations to match text1[0:i] with text2[0:j]
questions.explanation: dp[i][j] represents the length of the longest common subsequence considering the first i characters of text1 and first j characters of text2.

questions.question: In Edit Distance, if word1[i-1] == word2[j-1], what is dp[i][j]?
questions.explanation: When characters match, no operation is needed. We simply take the result from converting the prefixes without these matching characters: dp[i-1][j-1].

questions.question: Why do we iterate capacity BACKWARDS in space-optimized 0/1 Knapsack?
options: To prevent using the same item multiple times
questions.explanation: Iterating backwards ensures that when we compute dp[w], we use the old value of dp[w - weight[i]] (without current item), not an already-updated value that would count the item twice.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of the Unique Paths problem?
questions.explanation: We fill an m × n grid, computing each cell in O(1) time, giving O(m × n) total time.

questions.question: How can you find the Longest Palindromic Subsequence of string s?
options: Find LCS of s and s reversed
Use a single DP array iterating forward
questions.explanation: The longest subsequence that appears in both s and reverse(s) must read the same forwards and backwards, making it a palindrome.

questions.question: In Minimum Path Sum, what are the valid moves?
questions.explanation: The standard Minimum Path Sum problem only allows moving right or down, which is why the recurrence uses dp[i-1][j] (from above) and dp[i][j-1] (from left).

questions.question: What distinguishes Interval DP from regular 2D DP?
options: It uses intervals instead of indices
dp[i][j] represents an interval [i,j] and builds larger intervals from smaller ones
questions.explanation: In Interval DP, dp[i][j] represents the optimal solution for the subproblem defined by interval [i,j]. We fill by increasing interval length, combining smaller intervals.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of standard Edit Distance?
questions.explanation: Standard Edit Distance uses a 2D table of size (m+1) × (n+1), giving O(m × n) space. This can be optimized to O(min(m,n)).

questions.question: In Partition Equal Subset Sum, when can you immediately return False?
options: When the total sum is odd
When the array has only one element
questions.explanation: If the total sum is odd, it's impossible to partition into two equal parts. We need sum/2 to be an integer for the problem to have a solution.

questions.question: How do you handle obstacles in Unique Paths II?
options: Subtract obstacle count from final answer
questions.explanation: When a cell contains an obstacle, set dp[i][j] = 0 because no path can go through it. Paths must go around obstacles.

questions.question: What is the recurrence for Unique Paths?
questions.explanation: The number of ways to reach (i,j) is the sum of ways to reach the cell above (i-1,j) and the cell to the left (i,j-1), since you can only move right or down.

questions.question: In 0/1 Knapsack, what does dp[i][w] represent?
options: Whether item i fits in capacity w
Maximum value using items 0 to i-1 with capacity w
Number of ways to fill capacity w
Minimum items needed for capacity w
questions.explanation: dp[i][w] represents the maximum value achievable using the first i items with a knapsack capacity of w.
